_note: PROPOSAL. Nothing seeds unratified. Separate act from hygiene 7c(1), as ruled.
_origin: The sprinkler-tree master `03 Pumps/S02 Pumps- CSP.doc` yielded zero checklist rows but DID carry an eleven-field nameplate table. The husk was deleted; these fields were held out of that deletion and are proposed here on their own merits.
_existing: 37 defs, all duty-and-controller: pump type, rated flow/pressure/speed, driver, motor HP/V/FLA, controller type, engine make and BHP, fuel tank, battery arrangement, jockey pump setpoint.
_the_gap: fire_pump carries NO IDENTITY BLOCK AT ALL. It can describe what a fire pump is rated to do and cannot say which machine it is. Every other pump-family type carries Manufacturer / Model / Serial. This is the gap the master's table exposes, and it is the reason the fields are worth keeping rather than a reason to copy the table.

_what_was_NOT_proposed.why: already covered by the existing `Pump Type`

fire_pump carries `Motor Horsepower (HP)`. The table has a `unit_imperial` column, so kW/HP is a unit question on an existing field, not a new field. Adding both would print the same quantity twice in different units — the trim discipline that took heat_pump from 25 fields to 14.
table section labels in the source, not fields

add.why: No spec row: a specification names a basis of design, and the shop drawing is where the actual make is committed.
The master's own wording. Fire pumps are commonly identified by size as much as by model number.
Installed only — a serial number does not exist at spec or shop-drawing stage.

The as-built impeller determines the actual curve. `pump` already carries this at installed; fire_pump should carry it at both, because a trim change between shop drawing and installation is exactly the discrepancy the three-column layout exists to catch.
The one field of the five a specification genuinely does call out. Neither `pump` nor `fire_pump` carries it today.

_size: 10 def rows across 5 fields. fire_pump goes 37 → 47. Additive only; nothing existing is altered or removed.
